title: Complaint and mediation (Belgium)
subtitle: From the operator's complaint desk to the Telecommunications Ombudsman Service.
intro: The ombudsman service is a body of appeal set up at the BIPT. It does not replace your operator's customer service: it steps in when you got no satisfactory answer.
scope_note: This route covers a degradation as well as an outage. For the fixed scale owed after a total interruption of 8 hours or more, see the compensation module.
step.contact_operator: Contact your operator's complaint desk first.
step.keep_written_trace: Keep a written trace: dates, reference numbers, answers received.
step.wait_operator_answer: Wait for their answer, or note the absence of one.
step.file_written_complaint: File a written complaint with the ombudsman service. Only written complaints are admissible.
step.annex_prior_request: Attach your prior request to the operator and any answer it received.
step.await_outcome: The file is handled within 90 calendar days of the complete complaint, exceptionally extended once.
blocker.no_prior_contact: You have not contacted the operator first.
blocker.older_than_one_year: The complaint has been with the operator for more than a year.
blocker.court_case_pending: A case is already pending before the justice of the peace.
blocker.not_written: The complaint is not in writing.
admissible: No known obstacle. The ombudsman service assesses admissibility itself.
not_admissible: One or more obstacles would block the complaint:
evidence_note: Mire's readings are a solid body of indications for the discussion. They are not regulatory proof: article 4(4) of regulation 2015/2120 requires a monitoring mechanism approved by the national regulator, which Mire is not.
contact_body: Telecommunications Ombudsman Service, Boulevard Roi Albert II 8 box 3, 1000 Brussels. Phone 02 223 06 06.
verify: Deadlines and conditions must be verified on the ombudsman service website before you rely on them.
